sections.h2: What should a Vermont home seller know about the state's layout?
sections.html:
Vermont is a small, mostly rural state where real estate rules are handled town by town. It covers 9,623 square miles, is landlocked, and borders Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New York and Quebec.

The Green Mountains run north to south through the middle of the state. The Champlain Valley lies in the northwest along Lake Champlain, the Connecticut River Valley forms much of the eastern border, and the Northeast Kingdom is the rural northeast corner. Elevation runs from 95 feet at Lake Champlain to 4,400 feet at Mount Mansfield.

Vermont joined the Union on March 4, 1791 as the 14th state, after existing as the independent Vermont Republic from 1777. Montpelier is the capital and the least populous state capital in the country.

sections.h2: How many counties, cities and towns does Vermont have?
sections.html:
Vermont has 14 counties and 247 municipalities, made up of 237 towns and 10 cities, plus a handful of unincorporated areas. Incorporated villages sit inside towns, and the 2024 count is 30.

sections.h2: What does the Vermont economy look like around the housing market?
sections.html:
Vermont has the smallest state economy in the country, with a gross domestic product of $48.3 billion in 2025, and its sectors lean toward farming, forestry, tourism and health care. Dairy, forestry, maple syrup, wine and apples are major products, and Vermont produces about half of the nation's maple syrup.

The University of Vermont Medical Center is the largest employer, with more than 8,800 employees. GlobalFoundries was the largest private employer as of 2015, with about 3,000 workers in Essex Junction. Skiing and summer resort visits support tourism in many towns.

The Census Bureau puts the state's population at 644,663 for July 1, 2025, with 346,310 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied housing rate was 73.2 percent, the median value of owner-occupied homes was $316,600, median gross rent was $1,234 and median household income was $81,203.

sections.h2: How does climate affect a Vermont house sale?
sections.html:
Vermont has a humid continental climate with warm, humid summers and cold, snowy winters. The annual mean temperature is 43 degrees Fahrenheit, and annual snowfall ranges from 60 to 100 inches depending on elevation. The Northeast Kingdom often averages about 10 degrees colder than southern areas in winter.

For sellers, that means heating systems, roofs and driveways draw buyer questions. Water is a separate concern, covered next.

sections.h2: What flood disclosure does a Vermont seller owe?
sections.html:
Before or as part of a contract, the seller must give the buyer flood information under 27 V.S.A. § 380. That means a copy or link to the FEMA flood insurance rate map, a statement of any flooding or flood damage while the seller owned the property, and whether the seller carries or is required to carry flood insurance.

  • If the seller does not provide the information, the buyer may terminate the contract before title transfers or occupancy begins.
  • The buyer may sue for damages and attorney's fees, and may seek punitive damages if the failure was knowing.
  • A seller is not liable for an error that came from a public body or a licensed professional's written report that the seller reasonably believed was correct and passed on.
  • The law took effect June 17, 2024 and was amended effective September 1, 2025.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in Vermont?
sections.html:
Vermont property tax is a local grand list combined with a statewide education tax. Listers set values, towns bill and collect, and the Department of Taxes oversees the system.

The Department's 2025 report counts 328,613 properties and a municipal listed value of about $101.97 billion. All property pays education tax, and a property is treated as nonhomestead unless the owner files a homestead declaration. The 2024 nonhomestead rate was 1.391 percent. A seller in a town that has not been reappraised in years may find that the listed value sits well below the sale price: the report puts the 2024 statewide common level of appraisal at 72.36 percent.

Appeals begin with the listers and move to the board of civil authority and then to the state or Superior Court. The first board deadline is short, 14 days after the date of the listers' notice.

sections.h2: What transfer and recording steps apply to a sale anywhere in Vermont?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded in the land records of the town clerk where the property sits, and a property transfer tax return is filed with the sale. The tax is due within 30 days of the closing date.

  • Principal residence: 0.5 percent on the first $200,000, then 1.25 percent above, plus a 0.22 percent surcharge on the amount above $200,000.
  • Non-principal year-round home that is not a long-term rental: 3.40 percent, or 3.62 percent with the surcharge.
  • Nonresident seller: the buyer withholds 2.5 percent of the sale price on Form RW-171 within 30 days, unless the seller has a Commissioner's Certificate.

A 2025 town fee schedule lists recording at $15.00 per page and a flat $15.00 for a transfer tax return, and each town clerk can confirm local amounts. The Department reported $62.4 million in transfer tax and $31.1 million in withholding for fiscal year 2024.

sections.h2: How do probate, foreclosure and tax sales differ across Vermont?
sections.html:
The same state law applies everywhere, but filings go to the county where the person or property is located. A formal probate estate is opened in the Probate Division in the county where the person lived, when the person owned real estate or the estate is worth more than $45,000. An executor needs a license from the court to sell real estate, and the inventory is due within 30 days of appointment.

Tax sales follow 32 V.S.A. § 5252: the delinquency must be at least $1,500 and run more than a year, the collector must first offer a repayment plan, and the owner or lienholder can redeem within one year. Eviction cases go to the Civil Division of the Superior Court in the property's county.

Vermont estate tax applies only to estates of $5,000,000 or more, at 16 percent above that level.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale look like for a Vermont seller?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the mortgage approval step, but the Vermont paperwork still applies. The seller still gives flood information, the deed is still recorded with the town clerk, and the transfer tax return is still filed.

Sellers who consider a cash buyer often have an inherited house, a rental with tenants, back taxes or deferred repairs. Each of those has its own rules described in our statewide guides, and a buyer who purchases as-is does not change those legal steps. Talk with a Vermont attorney or title company about your house before signing anything.

faqs.q: How many counties does Vermont have?
faqs.a: Vermont has 14 counties. Chittenden County, with Burlington, is the most populous with 168,323 residents in the 2020 Census.

faqs.q: Where is a Vermont deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the town or city clerk where the property is located. A 2025 town fee schedule lists $15.00 per page for recording.

faqs.q: What is the Vermont property transfer tax?
faqs.a: For a principal residence it is 0.5 percent on the first $200,000 and 1.25 percent above, plus a 0.22 percent surcharge on the excess. It is due within 30 days of closing.

faqs.q: Do Vermont sellers have to disclose flood history?
faqs.a: Yes. 27 V.S.A. § 380 requires flood map information, flood history during the seller's ownership and flood insurance status.

faqs.q: Does Vermont have an estate tax?
faqs.a: Yes, at 16 percent on the Vermont taxable estate above $5,000,000. Smaller estates owe none.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Vermont house if I owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Tax due can be settled from the proceeds. A tax sale requires at least $1,500 delinquent for over a year and the owner may redeem within one year.
